issues.body: Section 3a declares heal_max_wait_minutes optional, specifies that absence means 10, and makes resolve()/queue_controls the single authoritative place applying that default. It separately requires a policy with no registry row to raise. But section 4a still requires a "malformed/absent heal_max_wait_minutes" to make the fleet rule raise. An absent field in an existing valid registry row is resolvable under the stated contract, so an implementation cannot satisfy both the resolver contract and this acceptance test. This is load-bearing: it decides whether a valid policy relying on the documented default produces queue metrics or fails every collection tick.
issues.fix_hint: Change the section 4a test to require malformed values and a missing/invalid registry row to raise, while an absent heal_max_wait_minutes field resolves to the authoritative default and feeds both sinks identically. If absence is instead intended to fail closed, remove the optional/default-10 contract everywhere and require the field explicitly.
issues.title: The fail-closed fleet self-test still contradicts the optional-field default

verdict.summary: The round-3 contradiction remains materially unchanged. Section 3a still defines heal_max_wait_minutes as optional, makes an absent field resolve to the authoritative default of 10, and distinguishes that case from an absent registry row. Section 4a's required self-test nevertheless says a malformed/absent heal_max_wait_minutes must make the fleet rule raise. Those contracts cannot both be implemented: a caller using the mandated shared resolver will validly receive 10 for an absent field, while the acceptance test requires that same case to fail the tick. The rest of the design is detailed and generally fail-closed, but this load-bearing threshold-provenance test remains internally inconsistent. Because the same major finding persists at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
